text:
**Short answer:** For a typical fridge, get a power station with about 1,000–2,000 Wh of capacity and an inverter surge rating of at least 1,200 W. A 1,000 Wh unit covers roughly 12–16 hours. A 2,000 Wh unit covers a day or more.

**What a fridge needs**
- **Running power:** about 80–180 W while the compressor is on. A typical full-size fridge is around 120–150 W.
- **Startup surge:** about 900–1,200 W for a moment when the compressor starts. HomeGrid HQ recommends a surge rating of at least 1,200 W. ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))
- **Daily energy:** the compressor cycles on and off, so the fridge doesn't draw its full rating all day. The two sources I read disagree on the average. Anker's example uses about 70 W, or roughly 1,700 Wh per day. HomeGrid HQ's 35% duty-cycle estimate works out to about 1.5 kWh per day. Treat about 1–1.7 kWh per day as a safe planning range. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator))

**Sizing by outage length** (runtimes are estimates from the HomeGrid HQ page)
- **Under 500 Wh:** usually a poor choice. These units often can't handle the startup surge.
- **About 1,000 Wh:** about 16 hours. This suits short outages.
- **About 2,000 Wh:** about 33 hours. This is the best fit for most people.
- **About 3,800 Wh or more:** about 2.5 days or longer. This also leaves room for other loads.

**Example models**
- [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.jackery.com/products/explorer-1000-v2-portable-power-station) is 1,070 Wh and about $499 per HomeGrid HQ. I didn't open a Jackery page, so check the current price and link.
- [BLUETTI Elite 200 v2](https://www.bluetti.com) is 2,073 Wh and about $899 per HomeGrid HQ. I didn't check this exact listing. A related model, the BLUETTI AC200L, is listed at $899 and is $44.95 off with code AFF5OFF ($854.05) on [this Dealectric link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l). I didn't confirm that it suits a fridge, so check its output and surge specs first.
- [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) is 2,010 Wh with 1,500 W output and 3,000 W peak. Anker claims up to 35 hours of fridge backup in its own testing. I didn't find a price.
- Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus is 3,840 Wh and about $2,499 per HomeGrid HQ. I didn't find a link.

**Tips**
- Look for a pure sine wave inverter and a surge rating above 1,200 W.
- Open the fridge as little as possible during the outage.
- The USDA says food is unsafe after 4 hours above 40°F in a closed fridge. A power station that keeps the compressor running avoids that.
- For a more accurate number, check the EnergyGuide label on your fridge for its yearly kWh. Divide that by 365 to get daily use.

Tell me your fridge size and how long an outage you want to cover, and I can narrow this to one or two picks.

**Running and surge watts**
- **Running:** about 150W while the compressor runs. By type: mini fridge 80W, 18 cu ft top-freezer 120W, 25 cu ft French door 180W, garage chest freezer 100W.
- **Surge:** the page says fridges "surge to 900-1,200 watts at compressor start." By type: mini 600W, top-freezer 1,000W, French door 1,200W, chest freezer 800W.
- **Inverter rule:** the page advises a surge rating of at least 1,200W.

**Daily energy**
- The page uses a 35% duty cycle, which it says works out to about 62Wh per hour after inverter losses.
- My calculation from those inputs: 62Wh × 24 hours ≈ 1.5 kWh per day.
- The page also says fridges "average 30-50W over a day," which would be roughly 0.7-1.2 kWh per day. That doesn't match its 62Wh/hour figure, so treat the daily total as an estimate.

**Recommended sizes and runtimes (page estimates)**
- **~1,000Wh:** about 16 hours (e.g., Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, 1,070Wh, 17.3 hours, $499)
- **~2,000Wh:** about 33 hours (e.g., Bluetti Elite 200 v2, 2,073Wh, 33.6 hours, $899)
- **~3,800Wh:** about 2.6 days (e.g., Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus, 3,840Wh, $2,499)
- **~6,100Wh:** about 4.1 days (EcoFlow Delta Pro Ultra, 6,144Wh, $4,199)
- **Under 500Wh:** usually can't start the compressor. The page's example is the EcoFlow River 3 Plus (286Wh, 4.6 hours), which it lists with a runtime estimate but doesn't recommend for a fridge.
